extracted.intended_audience: NLP / multimodal ML researchers and practitioners building or evaluating humor-understanding models (e.g., captioning, funniness ranking, explanation generation).
extracted.subtask_description: Benchmarks derived from The New Yorker Caption Contest for evaluating multimodal humor understanding via three tasks (matching, quality ranking, explanation). The dataset supports image+text instances, multiple splits (including from_pixels and from_description variants), and 5-fold cross-validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching task (caption recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model must recognize a caption written about a cartoon (vs. options that were not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances provide a list caption_choices and a correct label (e.g., 'C' means the 3rd choice is correct). Supported in both from_description and from_pixels settings. Example instance format included in dataset card. Use load_dataset(..., "matching") to access this split.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality ranking task (caption quality evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model must evaluate the quality of a caption by scoring it more highly than a lower-quality option from the same contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels indicate which choice is preferred (e.g., 'A' means first caption choice was rated higher). The dataset includes winner_source (e.g., 'official_winner') to indicate provenance of the winning caption. Available in both from_pixels and from_description variants; use ranking_from_pixels etc. to load image-based splits. Example instance format and label semantics are shown in the card.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation task (why a joke is funny)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model must explain why a given joke/caption is funny; the target is a natural-language explanation of the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The label is free-text (an explanatory paragraph) and serves as the autoregressive target for generation tasks. n_tokens_label is provided (example: 59 tokens). Available in explanation and explanation_from_pixels splits. Example instance and exemplar explanation given in dataset card.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label semantics and format per task
rubrics_metrics.description: Label fields' meaning depends on task: for matching/ranking labels are discrete choices (letters); for explanation the label is a free-text explanation. n_tokens_label records explanation length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset card gives concrete examples (e.g., 'The label "C" indicates that the 3rd choice is correct.'), and demonstrates how labels correspond to caption_choices or to explanatory text. Models and evaluation code must interpret label differently per task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instance fields and required data structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances include fields such as image, image_description, image_location, image_uncanny_description, from_description, entities, caption_choices, questions, instance_id, label, n_tokens_label, and (for ranking) winner_source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset card documents each field and provides example instances. Downstream systems should use image (PIL image) for from_pixels splits and textual fields for from_description splits; 'from_description' contains a combined scene/uncanny/entities description useful for text-only models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task variants: from_pixels vs from_description
rubrics_metrics.description: Each task is available in variants that either include the raw image pixels (from_pixels) or only the curated textual description (from_description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loading examples: load_dataset("jmhessel/newyorker_caption_contest", "ranking_from_pixels") or load_dataset(..., "ranking"). Choose the variant appropriate for unimodal or multimodal modeling. Many splits exist (matching_1..matching_4, explanation_4, etc.) to support cross-validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset splits and cross-validation setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Default provided splits include train/validation/test for several variants; initial reports used a 5-fold cross-validation setting with default split 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can access other splits (e.g., explanation_4) and specify which split to use. Example loading code is provided in the card. The dataset is relatively small and the card notes the 5-fold cross-validation setup used in original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation provenance and annotator payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotations were produced by a mix of crowdworkers and the paper's authors; crowdworkers were paid $15/hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full annotation process details are in the paper. This provenance info is relevant for assessing annotation quality and reproducibility; users are pointed to the paper for detailed methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation rationale and source combination
rubrics_metrics.description: The corpus combines three sources of data (see paper and referenced datasets) and adds curated cartoon-level annotations and joke explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the cited paper for full details of initial collection, normalization, and curation rationale. The dataset card lists upstream datasets and related citations that should be acknowledged when using the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and social-impact / bias considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is subjective and the jokes in the corpus may perpetuate negative stereotypes; images may contain adult themes and minor cartoon nudity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset card explicitly warns users to consider social impact and bias; users should take care when deploying models trained on this data and consult the paper for detailed discussion of limitations and biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal & sensitive information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal and sensitive information in the dataset has been redacted; original images are published in The New Yorker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The card states that images were originally published in The New Yorker and personal/sensitive information has been redacted. Users should still audit for residual sensitive content when using or releasing model outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and citation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The annotations provided by the authors are released under CC-BY-4.0. The dataset card requests that users cite the dataset and related papers when using the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The card includes full citation entries for the authors' paper and upstream datasets; it points to capcon.dev for more information and provides DOI/arXiv references. Users must comply with CC-BY-4.0 license terms and attribution requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended evaluation framing: challenge models to demonstrate multimodal humor understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset is explicitly framed to challenge AI models to 'demonstrate understanding' of sophisticated multimodal humor by capturing complex relationships between image and caption and allusions to human experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three tasks (matching, ranking, explanation) are chosen to be carefully circumscribed tasks where capturing subtle image-text relationships may suffice. Use this framing to design evaluation protocols and baselines appropriate to humor understanding rather than generic captioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usage notes and API examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset card provides code snippets and practical instructions for loading different task splits via the Hugging Face datasets API.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: from datasets import load_dataset; dset = load_dataset("jmhessel/newyorker_caption_contest", "matching"); or use ranking_from_pixels/explanation_from_pixels variants. The card also lists file formats (parquet) and available columns for inspection (Data Viewer).
